about: The salad meme is a reaction still of a woman in a striped top at a table with a bowl of salad, looking up with a look of disgusted disbelief, subtitled "Are you serious? Right in front of my salad?". Her outrage is wildly out of proportion to the thing she is guarding, and that is the joke: people use it to react to any small offense committed in their presence, as though it were a personal attack on their lunch.
origin: The line comes from a 2017 clip from an adult video site. The meme only circulates this safe-for-work reaction frame, and the absurd phrasing turned it into a general-purpose reaction.
usage:
The top box states the offense, usually starting with "really?" or "are you serious?", and the bottom box gives the "right in front of my X?" payoff. You can keep "salad" for the classic version or swap in something you care about.

It fits minor crimes witnessed in real time: someone microwaving fish at work, a merge conflict, a teammate stealing your kill, a sibling eating your leftovers. The pettier the offense, the better the overdramatic line works.
